name: Oman

campaign_state.basis: Two attacks on fuel storage in Oman were reported in March 2026 and none since. That is thin for a campaign, but the war they belong to has no reported end, so the classification stays uncertain and uncertain is treated as active.
campaign_state.limitation: One status search per system, in English, on 2026-11-11. 'Nothing found' after July 2026 means the declared queries returned no dated report, not that no attack occurred.

no_index_reason: No index is published for this country. The Monitored-Area ESDI's sector weights, decay horizons and transmission measure were built for a strike campaign and do not transfer (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §1-§3). This view shows reported major disruptions and energy-system context instead.

reporting_environment_text: Disruption is disclosed mainly through company and ministry statements, usually only when material to investors or the state.
reporting_note: Disruption becomes public mainly through statements by the ministry, the electricity regulator and state companies, carried by the national news agency and the press. No public event register was found, and the regulator's own documents could not be opened, so the coverage of this record cannot be computed.
comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

geography.note: 11 governorates, the count in both Natural Earth and the National Centre for Statistics and Information's bulletin (October 2026). Two Natural Earth codes are superseded and are joined by name, not by code. Official electricity production statistics use eight groupings, not these governorates.

rulings.note: Al Batinah North. Natural Earth keeps the code of the former undivided Al Batinah region; the current ISO code is OM-BS. Joined by name.

Musandam is not contiguous with the rest of Oman. It is drawn in two parts; the smaller is the wilayat of Madha, which belongs to this governorate. The area enclosed within Madha (Nahwa) is drawn with the United Arab Emirates.
Ash Sharqiyah South. Natural Earth keeps the code and the Arabic label of the former undivided Ash Sharqiyah region; the current ISO code is OM-SJ. Joined by name.

precision_policy.reason: Oman's governorates are large, but each of its coastal ones holds a single port-industrial area, so a governorate and a class together name the facility. While the 2026 war has no reported end, attacks and sabotage are recorded for the country, with no governorate, facility or operator. Other events are placed by governorate.

event_summary.note: Counts what was reported and found, not what occurred.

inclusion_threshold.applies_to: country systems only. Never applied to the Russia theatre corpus, which predates it and does not pass it (GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.2).
inclusion_threshold.rule: A publicly reported disruption to energy infrastructure that meets at least one clause below, supported by at least one source with a URL.

clauses.1: Refinery, gas-processing plant or LNG terminal shut down, or throughput materially cut, with the effect reported.
clauses.2: Export or import terminal operations suspended.
clauses.3: Trunk pipeline shut down, or force majeure declared on it.
clauses.4: A power plant of about 500 MW or more forced offline with a reported effect, or a generation shortfall that forced rotating outages.
clauses.5: A grid event affecting about 100,000 customers or more, or a grid-operator emergency declaration.
clauses.6: A coal-mine event that materially cut supply.
clauses.7: Production shut in at a reported, material volume.

exclusions: minor unit trips with no reported effect
policy decisions and sanctions with no physical effect (for example OPEC+ quota changes)
inferences from proximity to an event (a wildfire near a facility is not a disruption of it)
known_weaknesses: Absolute thresholds (500 MW, 100,000 customers) mean very different things in systems that differ in size by thirty times; a province-wide outage in a small province can fall below them.
'With reported effect' measures how much a country discloses as well as what happened.
One storm can produce several records; episodes are not yet grouped.
See GLOBAL_METHODOLOGY.md §5.1 for the full red-team.

episode_bases.named_hazard: The records name the same storm, flood, heat wave or other hazard.
episode_bases.explicit_common_event: A source explicitly says these records belong to one common event.
episode_bases.coordinated_wave: A source explicitly identifies these records as one coordinated attack or wave.
episode_bases.explicit_continuation: A later record reports the same operational disruption continuing.
episode_bases.singleton: No other record is tied to this one by a named hazard or an explicit common event.

review_summary.note: Blind reviewed (since iteration 17): three independent reviewers, none of whom saw the researcher's reasoning or each other, checked the evidence, the safety of the wording and the classification; all three accepted it. Dual reviewed: a researcher found the record and a second, independent reviewer opened its sources. Legacy: published before independent review was required, checked by one reviewer against the threshold and the scope scan; these are grandfathered by id and leave the list as they are re-reviewed.

profile.as_of_note: Compiled 2026-11-11 by the Oman source-audit lane (iteration 19, Wave A). A DRAFT in the local candidate queue. CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read from the cited document in this session; vintages differ (2024 and 2025) and are stated per row, and 2025 statistical values are marked provisional by their publisher. Bases differ by source (country totals from the National Centre for Statistics and Information, which credits the Ministry of Energy and Minerals and the Authority for Public Services Regulation; power-system figures from Nama Power and Water Procurement; a company total from Oman LNG) and are labelled on each row. Refining capacity and generating capacity were NOT read this session and are absent, not zero. National totals from the U.S. EIA are served by the global context layer and are not repeated here. No facility rows. See docs/countries/OM_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

significance: Oman produced an average of about 1.0 million barrels of oil per day in 2025 and exported about 308 million barrels in the year, equivalent to about 84% of production (National Centre for Statistics and Information, crediting the Ministry of Energy and Minerals; share computed).
Power generation used about 27% of Oman's gas supply in 2025 (National Centre for Statistics and Information; share computed from 15,494 of 57,056 million cubic metres).
Solar and wind projects supplied around 9% of electricity production in 2025, against a stated target of 30% by 2030 (Nama Power and Water Procurement).
Oman LNG reported LNG production of 11.98 million tonnes in 2024.
Oman has no coal production and no coal-fired generation (U.S. EIA International Energy Statistics, 2024, as committed in this repository's global context layer).

lanes.source_family: Ministry of Energy and Minerals statements and the national statistical bulletin, read for disruption-attributed changes
registry: Ministry of Energy and Minerals statements (Oman News Agency)
National Centre for Statistics and Information, Monthly Statistical Bulletin
lanes.finding: The bilingual bulletin is tables with definitional footnotes (provisional, coverage, source). Its oil and gas table (source: the ministry), refinery table (source: OQ) and electricity table (source: the regulator) carry no sentence that attributes a change to a disruption in any issue read. From 2024 the issues add infographic captions that state a percentage rise or fall (for example in total refinery output) with no cause: a numeric series with no attribution, so context and never an incident. No ministry statement of a disruption was reached by ordinary access. Zero candidates is a finding about the publication, not about the period.
lanes.limitation: The listing at ncsi.gov.om/publications?page=N is static but mixes all publication types at six per page with no working type filter, so the other issues were not located.

lanes.source_family: OQ group and PDO annual and sustainability reports and company releases
registry: Muscat Stock Exchange company disclosures (OQ Gas Networks, OQ Exploration and Production, listed power companies)
OQ group, OQ Exploration and Production, PDO (annual and sustainability reports); EIA; GCC-Stat
lanes.finding: The reports read are performance documents. They give company totals, safety statistics (recordable injuries, fatalities, counts of Tier 1 and Tier 2 process-safety incidents by year) and, for the upstream operator, a general aim of reducing 'deferments', with no date, place, cause or volume for any interruption. A count of process-safety incidents with no date and no effect is context, never an incident. Zero candidates is a property of what these publishers disclose.
lanes.limitation: Five of fourteen reports were read. Nine were not: four are over the fetch size limit, one timed out twice, two have links that resolve to cover images, and the two OQEP annual reports have no reachable address. The exchange's disclosure history and the gas-network company's investor pages remain unread.

lanes.source_family: Oman LNG annual reports, read for material interruptions of production
lanes.finding: The editions read report annual LNG output, a plant reliability percentage and a utilisation percentage for each of the last five years, and zero Tier 1 and Tier 2 process-safety events. They state no interruption, trip or cut of LNG production, and give no cause for any year-to-year change in utilisation. A reliability or utilisation series with no attribution is context, never an incident. Zero candidates is a finding about the publication.
lanes.limitation: Two of four editions were read, both in English. The 2022 edition is over the size limit in both languages and the 2025 edition returns no body text. Cargo, vessel and delivery passages were not recorded.

lanes.source_family: Power: procurement company reports and the regulator's findings on major interruptions
registry: Nama Power and Water Procurement: Annual Report and 7-Year Statement
Authority for Public Services Regulation statements and reports
lanes.finding: The procurement company's reports and statements describe demand, capacity planning and a reliability standard; none read states a past outage, blackout, generation shortfall or cyclone effect. For both, the regulator announced an investigation and no published findings document was found. No tropical-cyclone effect on electricity dated 2022-2025 with a customer or megawatt figure surfaced; the one cyclone figure met (about 120,000 customers) belongs to October 2021, before the window. A press report of the regulator's data lists nine investigated interruptions from 2014 to 2021, which shows the regulator does investigate such events; none of those is in the window.
lanes.limitation: Three of four declared queries were run, the cap; the English cyclone query was not. Two of four annual reports are over the fetch size limit and one 7-Year Statement issue is not listed. The regulator's site is unreadable, so whether it publishes investigation reports or interruption statistics is still not established; its statements were read only as the press carried them. No transmission-company document was read. The interconnection and reinforcement passages of the 7-Year Statements and all per-plant rows were not recorded.

lanes.source_family: Arabic and English media by year, via search
registry: Omani press: Oman Daily, Al-Watan, Al-Shabiba (Arabic); Oman Observer, Times of Oman, Muscat Daily (English)
International news agencies and energy press (Reuters, S&P Global)
lanes.finding: Storm reports give duration and pole counts, not customers. Local distribution cuts surface through a trade site quoting the distribution company's social-media statements. A discovery page gives counts and claims for later months;
lanes.limitation: Seven of twenty declared queries ran, all Arabic; no English query ran, so the lane is partial in language as well as in count. The year token barely filters: every power query returned the same 2022 and mid-2026 pages, and the fire strings returned no Omani refinery or gas-plant incident at all, so 2023 and 2024 are years in which the queries found nothing, not years shown to be quiet.

research_freshness.note: Research coverage describes the event search, not the sources: a country's sources can all be current while its search is unfinished, and a finished search can rest on a source whose own data is old. A fully executed search procedure is not complete knowledge: it means the declared sources were searched, not that nothing else happened.

recovery_coverage.policy: Observed recovery, or a sourced estimate labelled as an estimate. Nothing is modelled, and an event never ages out as recovered.

source_families.note: Which kinds of source the published events cite. Shows the reporting environment; it is not a quality score.

citation_quality.link_check_note: One automated visit to each cited page. Blocked means the site refused an automated visitor, not that the page is gone. Changed content needs an earlier visit to compare with, so this first run cannot report it.

monthly.rationale: three monthly releases missed, plus a month of publication lag

semiannual.rationale: two half-yearly releases missed, plus about a month of lag

annual.rationale: one annual release missed, plus about a month of lag

event_driven.rationale: no release cycle; the registry entry (access, licence, address) is re-checked at least twice a year
